title: Post-Expiry Stage Lengths, Domain Registrations
content:
# Post-Expiry Stage Lengths — Domain Registrations

Registry operations sheet giving, per TLD product of Domain Registrations, how long each stage after the expiry date lasts. Day counts are calendar days.

| TLD product | Renewal grace period (days after the expiry date) | Redemption Grace Period (days from the date the domain entered redemption) | Pending delete before purge (days) | DNS points to the Harborline renewal notice page from day | Paid restore offered in redemption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .us Domain Registration | 30 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .ca Domain Registration | 30 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .com Domain Registration | 30 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .org Domain Registration | 30 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .net Domain Registration | 30 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .co Domain Registration | 25 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| .io Domain Registration | 28 | 30 | 5 | 1 | Yes |

## Basis notes

- The renewal grace period is the number of calendar days after the expiry date during which the domain can still be renewed; the .co Domain Registration has 25 days and the .io Domain Registration 28 days, every other TLD product 30 days.
- The Redemption Grace Period is counted from the date the domain entered redemption and lasts 30 days on every TLD product.
- Pending delete lasts 5 days before the registry purges the name.
- Day 1 is the first day after the expiry date; from that day the domain's DNS points to the Harborline renewal notice page until the domain is renewed.

## Hypothetical comparison

Two hypothetical domains expire on the same day, one a .net Domain Registration and one a .co Domain Registration. The .net domain's renewal grace period runs for 30 days after the expiry date, the .co domain's for 25 days, so the .co domain reaches the end of its grace period five days earlier.
